optionalSupplies: Charity-shop finds for the acquisitions trip
substitutes: No spare plinths? Lay a folded towel on the floor for each exhibit.
title: After Hours at the Museum
clue: The gallery has closed to the public. One very special visitor has the place to themselves.
reveal: Your hallway becomes a gallery after closing time. Your dog tours five exhibits at their own pace, then meets one covered mystery piece. Whichever exhibit holds them longest earns a place in the permanent collection.
objective: Set up a five-exhibit gallery of safe objects, let your dog tour it freely, and give the favorite a place of honor.
instructions: Gather five clean, washable objects with different smells, each too big for your dog to fit in their mouth or swallow, with no loose parts, strings or threads: a folded fleece blanket, a bath towel, a cardboard tube, a silicone spatula too large to fit the mouth, a folded worn T-shirt. Wash anything second-hand first.

Set each on a 'plinth' (a folded towel or low upturned box) down a hallway or along a room edge, a stride apart on a non-slip floor. Then prepare the sixth exhibit, the mystery piece: a clean hand towel that has picked up an outdoor smell from a few minutes in your coat pocket on a walk or held at an open window. Fold a plain cloth over it and keep it out of sight until the end.
Dim the lights a little, but keep enough light to see. Announce 'the gallery is open' in your best curator voice, then follow two meters behind. No pointing, no steering.
Let your dog tour in any order and at any pace. They can sniff, nose, linger, skip any exhibit or leave. Watch which one holds them longest.
At the end, place the covered mystery piece on the last plinth and let your dog nose off the cover if they like.

Close the gallery with a quiet minute on the floor. Pick up every object. Put the favorite on a high shelf near their bed with a hand-lettered museum label ('Fleece, c. today. Favorite of the visitor').
twist: The last plinth is covered and holds a smell from outside the house, the only thing your dog has not met before.
variations: An acquisitions trip: spend a few coins in a charity shop on two or three large, chew-proof objects (a wool scarf, a canvas bag), wash them at home, and add them as new exhibits.

A gallery of firsts: replace the usual objects with five things your dog has never met (a clean fleece, a cardboard tube, a canvas tote, a hand towel from a friend's house, a cushion cover). No plants or food.

For a seated owner, a low-mobility dog, or a dog resting on your vet's advice (ask your vet first): set three exhibits within a few steps of the dog's bed, make it sniff-only with cloth and cardboard, and sit beside them.
For a puppy: use only towels and cardboard, keep it to two exhibits, and finish at the first sign of mouthing.
completion: Your dog has toured the gallery, or walked away from it, and you have chosen a favorite and given it a label.
photoIdea: Your dog at the plinth where they lingered longest, taken from the end of the hallway.
memoryPrompt: Which exhibit held your dog longest, and what did the label say?
supplies: Five clean, large, safe objects (towels, fleece, cardboard)
Towels or low boxes for plinths
Paper and a pen for the label
safety: Choose objects too big to swallow, with no strings, buttons or small parts.
If your dog starts chewing an exhibit, take it away and end with a rest.
